overview: Teotihuacan was a major urban center in central Mexico. Its public monuments, apartment compounds and specialized arts connected a large city with other Mesoamerican communities through exchange and influence.

items.text: The urban layout incorporated the San Juan River, whose course was altered to cross the Avenue of the Dead.
Builders used talud-tablero profiles, combining sloping and upright wall sections, in civil and religious architecture.
Apartment compounds grouped connected rooms around open courtyards. They provided durable shared housing for much of the city's population.
Murals decorated many buildings, especially residential compounds. Artists also made mold-pressed ceramics and geometric stone faces.
Imported craft goods included worked obsidian and Thin Orange pottery. Stackable bowls made long-distance transport more practical.
The Met's updated account places burning in the monumental core around 550 CE and marked population decline after 600. The people responsible are unidentified.
